payload.statement: His101 is the axial heme b ligand of gp91phox (CYBB). Replacing it with Arg removes the imidazole that coordinates the heme iron, so the heme cannot be held in the cytochrome b558 core and electron transfer from FAD to O2 fails.
payload.would_refute: The His101 side chain in the heme-bound cryo-EM structures (8WEJ, 8X2L, 7U8G) is not within coordination distance (about 2.5 Å) of the heme iron, or His101 is shown to be a non-coordinating residue. Equally, an Arg placed at 101 in a model that keeps the heme iron in place with a plausible ligand at the Arg position would weaken this hypothesis.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: UniProt annotates residue 101 as the axial heme b ligand (E3), and it is in the observed heme-bound structures (E15, E17, E18). This is the only evidence that ties the residue to a specific molecular function. It is still indirect: no paper or assay tests H101R (G1, G2, G4), and no structure carries the mutation (G3). Ranked above stability because E3 is residue-specific, while the stability evidence (E4, E8, E10, E11) only shows the residue is conserved and in a membrane helix.

payload.statement: His101 sits in the transmembrane helix (residues 96-130) of gp91phox. Inserting a charged Arg into the membrane-embedded helix destabilises the four-helix cytochrome b558 fold, so the protein misfolds, is degraded, and fails to mature with p22phox.
payload.would_refute: A stability calculation or MD run of the H101R model shows no significant destabilisation (for example ddG under about 1 kcal/mol, with the Arg side chain placed to avoid burial of charge). Or His101 is shown to be solvent-exposed and outside the membrane in the resolved structures, so it does not contribute to the helix packing.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: Conservation (E10 0.952), popEVE (E11), EVE (E13) and AlphaMissense (E8) all predict the substitution is damaging, and the residue lies in a TM helix (E4). These scores do not say why the change is damaging, and they do not separate folding loss from heme loss. The folding route is supported by E12 (p22phox maturation depends on the complex) but no direct data exists for this residue (G2, G4). Ranked second because it explains the same predictions as H1 without a residue-specific function.

payload.statement: His101 is at the gp91phox–p22phox heterodimer interface in the transmembrane region. The His-to-Arg change alters that contact, so p22phox cannot stabilise gp91phox, and the flavocytochrome b558 heterodimer does not form.
payload.would_refute: In the resolved NOX2–p22phox structures (8WEJ, 7U8G), no atom of His101 lies within about 4–5 Å of any p22phox residue, and the buried surface of the p22phox interface does not include residue 101.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: Only indirect evidence supports it: the complex-level structure (E5) and the deletion study of p22phox (E12) do not name residue 101. The interaction map does not tie any interaction to residue 101 (G5). Ranked last because no record item links this residue to p22phox contact, and the ligand route already has residue-specific annotation.

payload.summary: Three agent-generated hypotheses are recorded. H1 (ligand_binding, rank 1): loss of the axial heme ligand, supported by UniProt E3 and heme-bound structures E15, E17, E18. H2 (stability_folding, rank 2): TM helix destabilisation, supported by conservation and pathogenicity scores. H3 (protein_interaction, rank 3): loss of p22phox contact, with weak indirect support. The first test should check His101 distance to heme iron in 8WEJ, 8X2L and 7U8G, which refutes H1 if the coordination distance is not met. Gaps G1–G5 remain open, with no direct data for H101R.

payload.description: FoldX predicted folding free-energy change of His101Arg on the AlphaFold model, plus pLDDT at 101 and the same predictor for other substitutions at this residue. Discriminates H2 (destabilised fold, misfolding) from H1 (heme-ligand loss) and H3 (interface loss).
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: A destabilising value at or above the threshold (about 1 kcal/mol) would support H2 and raise it above H1, which is the current favourite. A neutral value would weaken H2, since H2's own refutation condition is ddG under about 1 kcal/mol, and would leave H1 and H3 in place. H1 and H3 are not directly moved by a stability value, so the change is mainly between H1 and H2. FoldX error is near 1 kcal/mol, so a borderline value would move the ranking very little.

The H101Y control (ddG -0.87 kcal/mol) only shows that FoldX calls both substitutions near-neutral. H1 stays at its starting support (E3, E15, E17, E18 place residue 101 at the heme site; E1, E8, E10, E20 are supporting).

agent-generated hypothesis. T1 predicts FoldX ddG -1.04 kcal/mol for H101R on AF-P04839-F1 (residue pLDDT 97.0), below the 2.0 kcal/mol destabilising threshold. This is numerically inside H2's refute range (ddG under about 1 kcal/mol), but I do not refute outright: H2's would_refute also requires the Arg side chain placed to avoid burial of charge, and that placement was not controlled. FoldX's error is near 1 kcal/mol, so the sign alone cannot exclude a modest destabilisation. The verdict is weakened, not refuted, pending a placement-controlled or MD check.

agent-generated hypothesis. T1 measures folding stability, not protein-protein contact. Its missense3d state was not_covered, and no p22phox interface atom distance was measured. T1 neither supports nor refutes H3; H3 keeps its starting support (E5, E12, E7, E9), which contains no residue-level interface measurement.

payload.uncertainty: T1 is a single FoldX prediction on the AlphaFold model (AF-P04839-F1), not on the experimental cryo-EM structures, and FoldX has errors near 1 kcal/mol, so a value of -1.04 cannot separate neutral from mildly destabilising. The control H101Y (-0.87 kcal/mol) shows the predictor gives near-neutral values at this residue regardless of substitution, so the test has little power at this site. No placement check of the Arg side chain or MD run was done, and T1 does not address heme coordination or the p22phox interface. A neutral ddG does not show the variant is tolerated: the clinical phenotype (E1, E2) and the high AlphaMissense/EVE scores (E8, E13) point to loss of function through a mechanism that FoldX does not model. Validation still needed: T2 (heme-iron distance in 8WEJ, 8X2L, 7U8G) and T3/T4 for the interface question, plus an experimental expression or maturation assay if available.

Favoured hypothesis stays H1 (heme axial ligand loss, agent-generated hypothesis), but it is still unconfirmed: its heme-iron distance criterion is untested. Next: run T2 ligand_contact (computational) to measure His101-to-heme-iron distance in 8WEJ, 8X2L and 7U8G.

payload.text:
## Question
For CYBB p.His101Arg (gp91phox, UniProt P04839), which molecular mechanism best explains loss of function, and does one targeted computational test change the conclusion? [E1] [E2]

## Evidence
ClinVar classifies the variant as pathogenic, with criteria provided and no conflicts [E1]. UniProt annotates residue 101 as an axial heme b binding site [E3], and cryo-EM structures 8WEJ, 8X2L and 7U8G observe residue 101 with heme bound [E15] [E17] [E18]. Computational predictors score the change as damaging: AlphaMissense 0.9975 [E8] and EVE 0.815 [E13]. These are predictions, not experimental results. No retrieved abstract names His101 [G1], and no functional assay covers residue 101 [G4].

## Agent-generated hypotheses
H1, ligand_binding (starting rank 1): loss of the heme axial ligand [H1]. H2, stability_folding (rank 2): destabilised transmembrane fold [H2]. H3, protein_interaction (rank 3): disrupted gp91phox–p22phox contact [H3]. All three are agent-generated hypotheses. H1 was favoured before the test [H1].

## Tests considered and the choice
Four candidates were considered: T1 stability_effect, expected learning 0.6, no approval, 0 compute seconds [T1]; T2 ligand_contact, 0.35 [T2]; T3 structural_context, 0.3 [T3]; T4 structure_comparison, not runnable and needs approval [T4]. T1 was chosen and cleared by safety. T2 to T4 were rejected with reasons [T1] [T2] [T3] [T4].

## Result
FoldX predicts a ΔΔG of −1.04 kcal/mol for H101R on the AlphaFold model, below the 2.0 kcal/mol destabilising threshold, with residue pLDDT 97.0 [T1] [E21]. The H101Y control gave −0.87 kcal/mol [E22]. This is a computational prediction and has not been validated experimentally.

## Updated decision
H1 remains favoured. H2 is weakened but not refuted, and H3 is unchanged [T1]. Favoured before: H1. Favoured after: H1. Decision changed: no [T1]. No reopening was needed, because the favoured hypothesis neither changed nor was weakened.

## Uncertainty and validation still needed
FoldX error is near 1 kcal/mol, and the H101Y control shows near-neutral values at this site, so the test has little power here [T1]. It used the AlphaFold model, not the cryo-EM structures [T1]. H1's refutation criterion, the heme-iron distance, has not been measured [H1]. The interface question for H3 is untested [H3]. No experimental expression or maturation data exist [G2] [G3].

## Next experiment
T2, a ligand-contact test: measure the His101 side-chain distance to the heme iron in 8WEJ, 8X2L and 7U8G [T2]. Prediction, not a result: the NE2 atom sits about 2.0–2.5 Å from the iron, which would support H1 [T2].
